arguments.count: DWORD count loaded once from original ESP+0C at entry, before either pointer home.
arguments.destination: DWORD destination home original ESP+04 loaded once after PUSH ESI/PUSH EDI, copied to ESI before zero-count branch.
arguments.source: DWORD source home original ESP+08 loaded once only on positive count at BFAEFF; zero count never reads source home.
arguments.return_value: EAX receives captured ESI destination at BFAF28 on every normal return, independent of later pointer-home changes; borrowed actual pointer/null, no ownership transfer.

count_zero.null_values: Null destination and source values require no pointed storage; destination is returned. Physical native argument/return stack still exists.

copy_phase.write: BFAF06 MOV WORD [EDI],AX through DS, before testing AX
copy_phase.progression: Each copied WORD increments EDI twice and EDX twice before TEST AX. These INC instructions advance forward irrespective of incoming DF.
copy_phase.nonzero: DEC ECX/JNZ after nonzero WORD. Exactly count nonzero WORDs exhaust count without an extra source read or padding.
copy_phase.zero: Copied zero WORD takes JZ before count decrement. TEST/DEC at BFAF15/BFAF19 accounts for that already-copied WORD; remaining padding count r=count-c, with c copied WORDs including zero.
copy_phase.overlap: Read current WORD before write current WORD, then advance. Genuine byte-level overlapping source/destination is not assumed disjoint: writes may change later reached source WORDs, including partial-byte overlap and the encountered zero position. No subsequent source reads after encountered zero.

padding.reached: Only after a copied zero and positive remaining r=count-c. r=0 skips both REP instructions.
padding.counts: SHR ECX,1 yields q=floor(r/2), CF=r&1; REP STOSD consumes q to ECX=0 without changing CF; ADC ECX,ECX then yields t=r&1; REP STOSW consumes t.
padding.entry_positions: Let P be the copy-phase EDI immediately after the copied zero. REP STOSD begins at offset P. With direction sign s=+1 for DF=0 or -1 for DF=1, its q stores have DWORD offsets P+s*4*j (j=0..q-1); REP STOSW begins at offset P+s*4*q and writes one WORD iff t=1. ES determines each padding destination interpretation; no DS/ES equality is established.
padding.widths: q DWORD stores followed by t WORD stores, not an established sequence of r WORD stores.
padding.DF: No CLD/STD. Incoming DF is not established or restored by this body; padding direction depends on it. Copy-phase MOV stores use DS, padding string stores ES.
padding.scope: Register-offset description of actual instructions only. No general physical alias/fault/segmentation contract or successful-storage proof is recovered.
